evals.expected_output: Reads the staged diff and recent git log, detects the convention, and writes an imperative subject naming the effect plus a body explaining why, with the command to apply it.
expectations: Reads git diff --cached rather than unstaged changes
Matches the style found in recent git log subjects
Subject is imperative, under 72 characters, and names the effect
Does not run git commit unless asked

evals.prompt: I've staged a bug fix, a dependency upgrade, and a bunch of formatting. Just commit it all as 'updates'.
evals.expected_output: Explains why 'updates' and a mixed commit hurt review, revert, and bisect, proposes splitting into three commits with exact commands, and offers to proceed either way.
expectations: Gives exact git restore --staged / git add commands
Suggests meaningful subjects for each commit

evals.prompt: Write the commit for this change that removes the deprecated /v1/users endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Writes a message that clearly marks the breaking change (BREAKING CHANGE footer in a Conventional Commits repo, or an explicit body line) with what clients must do instead.
expectations: Says what consumers should use instead
Body explains why the endpoint was removed
